root: generative pipeline for discovery of single phase immersion coolants
gaps: No programme measures the card's exact quantity: whether the best MD-ranked coolant's cooling FOM keeps improving as the number of MD-verified candidates grows from ~100 to ~1000 (vs. plateauing).

Ewen group's MD verification covers only 8 representative molecules with no immersion-coolant FOM compared against commercial fluids; Sinton/FL01 verify experimentally and via CFD, not with MD; Org-Mol never MD-verified its shortlist.

Activity of the Org-Mol/SINOPEC team is inferred from a July 2025 paper plus multi-year funding; no follow-on release was found by Oct 2026, so its 'active' state is weaker evidence than for the Ewen (Sep 2026 paper) and Sinton/FL01 (Nov 2025 launch, Sep 2026 prototyping) programmes.

programmes.name: Ewen group (Imperial College London / University of Bath) — MD benchmarking of organic-liquid thermophysical properties
programmes.step: The GPU molecular-dynamics verification of candidate fluids' viscosity and thermal conductivity — the exact step the card scales to 100/300/1000 candidates. Today the group runs equilibrium MD (EMD) on a handful of representative molecules and benchmarks it against ML predictors for density, viscosity and thermal conductivity of C10–C50 organics (lubricants and cooling fluids).

activity.claim: Most recent output is the Digital Discovery paper benchmarking ML vs MD for organic-liquid thermophysical properties, dated 29 Sep 2026, following a 22 Apr 2026 ChemRxiv preprint on the hydrocarbon version.

claims.claim: The group's ML-first screening toolchain is built on a ~4,700-value experimental database for 835 organic molecules, with XGBoost as the best model — i.e. MD is used only as a spot-check, not at screening scale.

MD verification is run on only eight molecules, and the group already concluded that ML (orders of magnitude cheaper than EMD) is the right tool for high-throughput screening — the assumption the card tests.

The work is done by Egheosa Ogbomo, Fionn Carman, Daniele Dini and James Patrick Ewen (Imperial College London; Ewen now Lecturer at University of Bath), using supercomputer molecular simulation of solid-liquid interfaces.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If the best MD-ranked coolant keeps improving as verified candidates grow 100→1000, the group has a concrete reason to build a GPU-MD verification stage as a genuine ranking/filter (not an 8-molecule benchmark), investing in throughput and force-field refinement so MD — rather than XGBoost alone — decides which candidates advance.
programmes.if_not_changes: If the best FOM plateaus by a few hundred candidates, it confirms their published conclusion that ML predictors at orders-of-magnitude lower cost are the right screening tool and that MD's force-field error (~chemistry-dependent bias in viscosity/thermal conductivity) caps its ranking value; their MD stays a spot-check rather than a scaled verification layer.

already_done.claim: They have EMD-verified thermophysical properties but only for a fixed set of eight representative molecules; they have not run the card's scaling experiment (best MD-ranked FOM vs number of MD-verified candidates from 100 to 1000, compared to commercial fluids).

programmes.name: Sinton Lab / FL01 (University of Toronto + Acceleration Consortium) — self-driving lab for immersion coolant discovery
programmes.step: The verification/ranking of many candidate coolants — the same pipeline stage the card runs with GPU-MD, which Sinton/FL01 run instead with a wet-lab self-driving lab measuring viscosity, density, heat capacity, thermal conductivity and dielectric constant.

activity.claim: FL01 launched November 2025 and, as of a 1 Sep 2026 Acceleration Consortium article, is prototyping its self-driving lab with several industry partners.

claims.claim: Their verification throughput is 5 samples/hour (claimed 100× conventional), i.e. thousands of measurements per device per month, but still a wet-lab loop rather than computation.
Data-generation scale is the explicit selling point: one device produces 10,000 data points in two months, versus ~4,000 publicly available data points over the prior century.

The group already uses a figure of merit (FOM) for immersion coolants and screens >1600 fluid mixtures by coupling CFD with active learning (15 data points to drive the FOM, 10× efficiency). People: David Sinton, Mohammad Zargartalebi, Hanie Rezaei, Maryam Ebrahimiazar (U of T Mechanical & Industrial Engineering); FL01 CEO Zargartalebi.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If more MD verification keeps raising the best FOM, FL01/Sinton gains a cheap GPU pre-filter: MD could rank a million candidates before any fluid is ever synthesized, letting their 5-samples/hour wet-lab loop spend effort only on the MD-verified top tier — shrinking the 'years to weeks' R&D timeline further and de-risking which chemistries to buy/synthesize.
programmes.if_not_changes: If MD FOM plateaus, their experimental self-driving lab remains the only trustworthy verifier (their Nature Communications microfluidic method already argues computational thermal-conductivity models carry ~10% errors and 'necessitate experimental verification'), so they keep investing in sensor/SDL throughput rather than GPU-MD, and the card's MD stage is not added to their loop.

already_done.claim: Sinton/FL01 verify and rank candidates experimentally (self-driving lab, microfluidics, CFD+active learning), not via GPU molecular dynamics, and they have not run the card's MD-verification scaling experiment (best MD-ranked FOM vs number of MD-verified candidates).

opencode-go/minimax-m3: Card measures computational MD-FOM as stand-in for their experimental wet-lab verification; bridges computation to experiment.

programmes.name: Org-Mol team (SINOPEC Research Institute of Petroleum Processing + DP Technology + AI for Science Institute)
programmes.step: The post-ML-filter down-selection the card replaces with MD verification: Org-Mol ML-screens millions of esters, filters to a 461-candidate shortlist, then manually picks only two to synthesize and measure — exactly where the card would insert GPU-MD verification of the top 100–1000.

activity.claim: The pipeline was published 11 July 2025 and is backed by multi-year funding from China Petroleum & Chemical Corp and the National Key R&D Program of China (grant 2024YFA1510200), indicating an ongoing effort rather than an archived one.

claims.claim: Generation + ML filter runs at millions scale: >6 million saturated mono-/dibasic esters are constructed and screened by dielectric constant, yielding 8569 monoesters.

The downstream filter collapses the shortlist to 461 by predicted viscosity and thermal conductivity, then to 2 by human synthetic-feasibility judgement — no computational verification of hundreds of candidates exists.

People/institutions: Qi Ou, Minyang Zhuang, Lele Liu, Ning Wang (SINOPEC Research Institute of Petroleum Processing, Beijing); Hongshuai Wang, Shangqian Chen, Zhifeng Gao (DP Technology, Beijing); Zhifeng Gao (AI for Science Institute, Beijing). The model is a Uni-Mol-derived 3D transformer (Org-Mol).

programmes.if_lever_changes: If MD verification keeps raising the best FOM, the Org-Mol pipeline would add a GPU-MD verification stage (100–1000 candidates) between the 461-candidate ML shortlist and synthesis, replacing the manual 2-candidate pick with an MD-ranked list — likely producing a verified coolant that beats commercial fluids and turning their 'two validated candidates' proof-of-concept into a scalable discovery engine.
programmes.if_not_changes: If MD FOM plateaus, their current practice is confirmed as already near-optimal: ML filtering to a few hundred then hand-picking two to synthesize is sufficient, and spending compute on MD-verifying hundreds-to-thousands of candidates would be a waste, so the pipeline stays ML-plus-sparse-experiment.

already_done.claim: Org-Mol ML-screened millions of esters and experimentally validated two synthesized candidates; it never MD-verified hundreds-to-thousands of candidates' viscosity and thermal conductivity, so the card's scaling experiment has not been run by this team.
